title: GPU driver rollout safety checklist and experiment plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a safety-first checklist and experimental plan to validate GPU driver and CUDA runtime rollouts across our primary cloud SKUs (A100, H100, L40S). It collects the set of minimal smoke checks, perf regressions, soak tests, and rollback criteria we require before a staged rollout to production.

Scope:
- Driver binaries (NVIDIA driver versions) and CUDA/cuDNN/cuBLAS stacks.
- Cloud SKUs we care about: aws-cuX (pX.*), gcp-* (a100/h100), azure-l40s.* and equivalents.
- Workloads: short-text regen (low token), long-context streaming, large-batch embedding throughput, and multi-tenant packing microbursts.
- Excludes OS kernel updates and custom hypervisor patches (handled by infra team).

Motivation / why this checklist exists (observed failure modes):
- First-request variance: long driver init or module binding increases 1st-token latency under cold pools.
- Unexpected regressions in cuBLAS kernels impacting FP16/INT8 perf on certain driver versions.
- NVLink initialization stalls and multi-GPU collective hang risk during model load.
- Subtle power/clock-stepping differences causing drift in long-soak throughput.
- Silent increases in p99/p999 even when p50 looks stable (tail amplification).

High-level rollout strategy:
1) Local dev validation (single-node lab machines)
2) Staging canary (isolated VPC, limited routes, dedicated gpu pool)
3) Small production canary (5% traffic, dedicated tenant)
4) Ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers

Minimum acceptance metrics (for each SKU & driver combo):
- Correctness: no CUDA errors in logs, no target-exit codes, successful model init for all model variants.
- Functionality: identical text outputs on targeted smoke prompts (seeded RNG where relevant) within tolerance.
- Latency: p50 within ±5% of baseline, p95 within ±7%, p99 within ±10%.
- First-token latency: < 1.5x baseline for cold workers.
- Throughput: bulk embeddings throughput within ±10% of baseline for steady-state long-run test.
- Resource/health: GPU util within expected range, no increased ECC/thermal/power alarms, no OOMs.
- Stability: no new OOM/segfault/TDR events during 24h soak in staging.

Key telemetry to capture (per test run):
- Per-request: request_id, route, model, sequence_length, batch_size, tokens_out, p50/p95/p99 latency buckets, first_token_latency.
- Host/GPU: driver version, CUDA version, kernel ring buffer, GPU temperature, power draw, clock speeds, PCI topology (NVLink lanes), GPU memory usage, nvml errors.
- Serving runtime: KV cache hit/miss, batch sizes, queue depth, time-in-queue histogram.
- Low-level traces: cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel time breakdowns (where feasible), profiler traces (Nsight or nvprof summaries).

Experiment test matrix (recommended minimal coverage):
- Drivers: current-stable (baseline), candidate-1, candidate-2 (most common + latest major).
- CUDA toolkits: baseline CUDA matched to candidate, and one mismatch scenario (candidate driver + older CUDA) to surface compatibility issues.
- SKUs: A100-gpu (single socket), H100-gpu (single socket), L40S (single socket), and the most-used VM families on each cloud provider.
- Workloads: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-context streaming (1k+ tokens), embedding batches (batch sizes 1, 16, 64, 256), mixed-tenant microburst (sequences of short low-latency requests).

Run types and duration:
- Smoke: 30m single-run per config, functional + light perf.
- Perf microbench: repeated tests to measure median and tails (typically 1–3 hours with repeated bursts).
- Soak: 24 hours running representative traffic mix to detect drift, clocks, thermal throttling.
- Edge-case stress: multi-GPU collective loads and model loading concurrency tests (30–120 minutes).

Detailed checklist (pre-test):
- [ ] Build a reproducible AMI/VM image description with exact driver and toolkit versions captured.
- [ ] Create test routes in staging and bind them to dedicated GPU pools.
- [ ] Tag baseline artifacts and collect baseline perf traces for each SKU.
- [ ] Confirm metrics collection pipelines (datadog/prometheus/jaeger) accept the new telemetry fields.
- [ ] Reserve infra windows and notify SRE/infra on-call.

Smoke test steps:
1) Deploy driver on isolated staging fleet (1-2 nodes per SKU).
2) Run correctness suite: model init, small inference samples, embedding checksums.
3) Run 30m controlled workload: record p50/p95/p99 and first-token latency.
4) Inspect host logs for CUDA-related warnings (soft ECC, NVML warnings, driver binding errors).

Perf and tail analysis steps:
- Collect histograms for p50/p95/p99/p999. Use a fixed set of synthetic workloads plus a sample of real traffic replay.
- Run kernel-level sampling for slow requests to attribute to cuBLAS/cuDNN or runtime queuing.
- Compare distributions vs baseline and produce a delta report (percentiles and sample size).

Soak and stability steps:
- Run 24h soak with representative multi-tenant mix. Monitor for: drift in latency, periodic spikes, OOMs, TDRs, ECC counts.
- Run nightly extended soak (72h) for candidates we plan to promote.

Rollout gates and automatic rollback triggers (examples):
- Immediate rollback if any of: segfaults, TDRs, repeated NVML driver load failures, or correctness regressions in smoke tests.
- Rollback if p95 regresses > 10% or p99 regresses > 15% and keeps trending for 30 minutes during canary.
- Rollback if GPU ECC or thermal alarms increase by > 50% over baseline in staging.

Safety mitigations and fallbacks:
- Maintain a pool of warm fallback workers pinned to baseline driver for fast traffic failover.
- Canary only a small subset of tenants (internal + low-risk first) before opening to external customers.
- Enable auto-failover routing in the console to reroute to baseline model variants if availability drops below SLA.

Artifacts to produce for each driver candidate:
- Short summary: 1-page pass/fail + key percentiles and any blocking items.
- CSV with per-request latencies and tags.
- Kernel sample summaries and largest-kernel attribution.
- NVML logs and dmesg extracts.
- Soak stability report and list of anomalies.

Analysis checklist (post-run):
- [ ] Verify no new error classes in logs; search for common substrings that indicate driver-level faults.
- [ ] Compare flame graphs / kernel attributions against baseline; highlight top-3 regressions.
- [ ] Confirm deterministic reproduction steps for any regression.
- [ ] Document mitigation work (tuning, driver flag, model fallback) and re-run targeted microbench.

Operational playbook (quick steps if rollout causes issues):
1) Pause rollout and stop further canary expansion.
2) Reroute traffic away from canary pool to baseline pool via control plane.
3) Collect fresh diagnostic bundle (logs, nvml, dmesg, perf samples) and open INF incident.
4) If issue is driver-level and reproduces on staging, roll entire canary pool back to baseline driver image and sandbox the candidate image for debug.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Determine a concise set of synthetic seeds that surface cuBLAS regressions deterministically (Diego).
- Add automated profiling capture for top 10 slow requests in the runtime (Priya to prototype).
- Decide acceptable p99 window for short-chat routes (proposal: +10% absolute limit).

Owners & sign-offs:
- Experiment owner: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE point: Oliver Park
- Infra / AMI build: Ruth Nakamura
- Release sign-off: Eng Director + SRE on-call

Appendix: quick commands and notes
- Collect nvml summary: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,power.draw --format=csv -l 1
- Capture dmesg and filter: dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|cuda|nvlink|nvrm_corruption" > /tmp/dmesg.driver.log
- Profile a slow request: run nsight sampling for the request stack and collect cuBLAS kernel timings (see internal profiler runbook).

This checklist is intentionally conservative. The goal is to expose subtle regressions early and provide a repeatable, low-risk path to promote driver updates across our SKUs.

Notes to reviewers: add missing test cases you think expose driver/CUDA compatibility issues (especially for mixed-precision and MIG). If you sign off on this plan, we will schedule a staged rollout window in the next infra maintenance cycle.
